newsitem.title: FRANCE: Axa-UAP profits helped by life activities.
newsitem.headline: Axa-UAP profits helped by life activities.

text.p: Axa-UAP, which reported on Wednesday a 39.5 percent jump in 1996 net attributable profit to 2.73 billion francs, said performance was driven by life insurance results, due to a strong improvement in the United States, France and the United Kingdom.

The performance was also lifted by property and casualty insurance results which increased strongly in France, Belgium and Britain. The exception was Axa Global Risks in Britain which posted losses due to the strengthening of reserves related to claims which occured prior to 1992.
First time full year consoldiation of National Mutual, consolidated for one month only in 1995, also helped boost profits.

There was a strong increase in net income from U.S. finanancial services -- DLJ and Alliance Capital Management -- and there was a strong contribution from the holding company thanks to "very good investment results."
There were also extraordinary profits due to changes in local accounting methods in life insurance at the level of the Dutch and Canadian subsidiaries.
Factors having a negative impact on profits included losses from Axa Leben life insurance unit in Germany and losses from French real estate subsidiaries due to real estate valuation allowances.
